name: Roasting chiles
tile_uses: Stuffed chiles, tacos, the weekend fish
why_now: Poblanos, Anaheims, and Hatch chiles come in together in late August and are gone by mid-October. This is the short window when they are everywhere, cheap, and often being roasted in a drum outside the market. Nothing else in the year replaces them.
how_to_choose: Firm, glossy, and heavy for their size
Flat-ish sides char more evenly than deeply lobed ones
Poblano for stuffing — wide shoulders, thick walls
Anaheim or Hatch for strips — longer, thinner, milder
Skip anything wrinkled or light; it has been sitting
buy_this_much: 6–8 for the week. They lose about half their volume once roasted and peeled, so this is less than it looks.
price_note: Cheapest they will be all year, and cheaper still by the sack. If a market is roasting them on site, that price usually beats buying them raw and doing it yourself.

flavor_paths.name: Rajas
flavor_paths.description: Roasted, peeled, torn into strips. The smoky flavor.

flavor_paths.name: Stuffed
flavor_paths.description: Whole poblanos with picadillo or jack, in tomato broth.

flavor_paths.name: As a paste
flavor_paths.description: Blended with garlic, lime, and oil for the fish.

weekday_uses: Strips in tacos and rice bowls
Blended into the paste for the fish
On the sheet pan with delicata
weekend_use: Blended with garlic and lime into the paste for the chile-rubbed mahi-mahi.
storage: Whole and raw, a week in the crisper. Roasted and peeled, four days in the fridge in a covered container, or freeze them in strips — they freeze better than almost any other vegetable in this basket.
one_thing_to_learn: Charring a chile is not about cooking it. It is about destroying the skin, which is thin, papery, and unpleasant to eat, so that what is underneath can be. That is also why the covered fifteen minutes after charring matters more than the char itself: the trapped steam separates skin from flesh. Skip the steam and you will spend ten minutes scraping. Do it, and the skin slips off in sheets.
market_question: Are these Hatch, or grown here? And how hot is this batch?
